state.objective: Seal Can's browser runtime so production browser bundles resolve zero Node builtin modules, keep all Can semantic guarantees intact, freeze type/error identities and source locations during the build, and leave assertion context out of the shipped bytes. The consultation compares implementation mechanisms for that fixed goal; no response alters the required observable behavior.
state.baseline: Nine runtime files form the core: data, domain, failure, completion, diagnostics, entry, callable, coordination, owner. They currently touch Node type predicates, sync hashing, sync file reads, ambient async context, assertion values, and Bun/process entry points. Bun's suite pins exact hostile-proxy behavior including zero trap execution. Compatibility with old spellings is not a requirement.
state.proxy_evidence: Probes establish that standard JavaScript offers no trap-free proxy test: the Node helpers are engine-internal, and Array.isArray sees through array targets. Bun regression tests pin zero-trap rejection on several hostile-proxy paths. A single shared file therefore cannot satisfy both the Bun pins and a Node-free browser graph; the browser implementation must accept bounded contained trap firing while still rejecting foreign values, never touching getters, and never serializing native causes.
state.hash_evidence: Identity sealing today is a synchronous hash comparison with pinned forgery rejection. Since browsers hash asynchronously and custom hash code is prohibited, the browser path needs startup-time async verification ahead of all domain usage plus a creation gate on verified plans. Manifest coverage of plan bytes arrives in a follow-up build task.
state.assert_evidence: Assertion values flow through coordination/callable paths whose identity layer depends on Node crypto, yet the browser product must ship none of it and must execute on explicit owner context. Browser-specific coordination and callable modules must therefore cut assertion imports, replacing digest identities with deterministic local counters and removing assertion parameters outright.
state.contract: Non-negotiable constraints: one shared portable core plus minimal per-host adapters, no parallel runtime rewrite and no phony Node shims, active fail-closed rejection of foreign/proxy values, assertion-gated build selection preserved, and diagnostics limited to category, phase and Can source coordinates without native or secret data. Module inventory edits land via the coordinator.

profile_structure.instructions: How should the browser profile relate to the Bun runtime sources?

criteria.seam_plus_overlay: Unify predicate-only modules on canonical files with a host-chosen predicate seam, author alternate browser modules only for divergent machinery such as hashing, loaders, ambient state, assertion plumbing and startup, and apply a documented specifier overlay at browser bundle time.
criteria.full_duplication: Maintain two complete copies of the core runtime, one per host, synchronized only by parallel tests.
criteria.node_alias_shims: Map Node builtin specifiers to browser polyfills during bundling and leave runtime sources untouched.
criteria.weaken_bun: Converge both hosts on portable code by downgrading Bun's proxy rejection promises and editing current tests to match.

identity_sealing.instructions: How must the browser profile establish sealed type and error identities?

criteria.async_startup_verify: Check every sealed identity asynchronously before first domain use, admit only verified plans afterwards, and layer build-manifest digests on top in the follow-up task.
criteria.trust_manifest_only: Omit plan verification from the browser runtime, leaving forgery detection to build-time digests alone.
criteria.sync_hand_hash: Reimplement hashing synchronously in maintained TypeScript for the browser profile.

assert_surface.instructions: What belongs in the shipped profile where Bun uses assertion values?

criteria.assert_free_variants: Cut assertion imports and parameters from the browser variants, identify receipts with local counters, and verify assertions during the build instead of shipping the machinery.
criteria.fail_closed_stubs: Bundle inert assertion stubs that fail any assertion operation at runtime.
criteria.ship_full_assert: Carry the full assertion system into shipped browser code.
